subject: Checking CLPM syntax for possible design errors

messages.author: f1797a55f5f3c31f
messages.subject: Checking CLPM syntax for possible design errors
parts:
Hello everyone!

Recently, I have been building a cross-lagged panel model. Data seems good, it runs without errors, invariance seems good, it has good fit and the results look plausible. However, I really wanted to check if there are no mistakes I made in the model syntax, as this is the first such model I made and I can imagine I might have misunderstood something.

Below, I have put an abbreviated script that contains all the elements of my model. This model contains:
- Three endogenous variables, measured at 5 time points, of which:
    - One of them ('endo1') is a latent variable with ordinal indicators (five outcome categories)
    - One of them ('endo2') is a binary observed variable
    - One of them ('endo3') is a continuous observed variable
- One unchanging exogenous variable ('tic1'), measured only at t1 (a time-invariant covariate)

I tested measurement invariance step-by-step and that seemed all good (factor loadings, intercepts, thresholds). In the same way, I tested the equality constraints on the regression coefficients, which also held up.

In short, I have two questions:
1. Are there any clear mistakes in the syntax below? Did I misunderstand how to do anything?
2. When constraining the intercepts to equality over time, can I leave the intercepts of t1 alone? These variables are not exogenous (only due to the sole effect from the TIC) but their intercepts are of course very different from those of t2 to t5. It would seem strange to try to include them in the equality constraints.



model.1 <- '

########################################
### MEASUREMENT MODEL ###

# ENDOGENOUS LATENT VARIABLE 'endo1' WITH ORDINAL OVs
# [Fixed factor loading of first indicator to 1.]

endo1_t1 =~ 1*ov1_t1 + lmb1*ov2_t1 + lmb2*ov3_t1
endo1_t2 =~ 1*ov1_t2 + lmb1*ov2_t2 + lmb2*ov3_t2
endo1_t3 =~ 1*ov1_t3 + lmb1*ov2_t3 + lmb2*ov3_t3
endo1_t4 =~ 1*ov1_t4 + lmb1*ov2_t4 + lmb2*ov3_t4
endo1_t5 =~ 1*ov1_t5 + lmb1*ov2_t5 + lmb2*ov3_t5

# THRESHOLDS OV

ov1_t1 | tau_a1*t1 + tau_a2*t2 + tau_a3*t3 + tau_a4*t4
ov1_t2 | tau_a1*t1 + tau_a2*t2 + tau_a3*t3 + tau_a4*t4
ov1_t3 | tau_a1*t1 + tau_a2*t2 + tau_a3*t3 + tau_a4*t4
ov1_t4 | tau_a1*t1 + tau_a2*t2 + tau_a3*t3 + tau_a4*t4
ov1_t5 | tau_a1*t1 + tau_a2*t2 + tau_a3*t3 + tau_a4*t4

ov2_t1 | tau_b1*t1 + tau_b2*t2 + tau_b3*t3 + tau_b4*t4
ov2_t2 | tau_b1*t1 + tau_b2*t2 + tau_b3*t3 + tau_b4*t4
ov2_t3 | tau_b1*t1 + tau_b2*t2 + tau_b3*t3 + tau_b4*t4
ov2_t4 | tau_b1*t1 + tau_b2*t2 + tau_b3*t3 + tau_b4*t4
ov2_t5 | tau_b1*t1 + tau_b2*t2 + tau_b3*t3 + tau_b4*t4

ov3_t1 | tau_c1*t1 + tau_c2*t2 + tau_c3*t3 + tau_c4*t4
ov3_t2 | tau_c1*t1 + tau_c2*t2 + tau_c3*t3 + tau_c4*t4
ov3_t3 | tau_c1*t1 + tau_c2*t2 + tau_c3*t3 + tau_c4*t4
ov3_t4 | tau_c1*t1 + tau_c2*t2 + tau_c3*t3 + tau_c4*t4
ov3_t5 | tau_c1*t1 + tau_c2*t2 + tau_c3*t3 + tau_c4*t4

# COVARIANCES

ov1_t1 ~~ ov1_t2 + ov1_t3 + ov1_t4 + ov1_t5
ov1_t2 ~~ ov1_t3 + ov1_t4 + ov1_t5
ov1_t3 ~~ ov1_t4 + ov1_t5
ov1_t4 ~~ ov1_t5

ov2_t1 ~~ ov2_t2 + ov2_t3 + ov2_t4 + ov2_t5
ov2_t2 ~~ ov2_t3 + ov2_t4 + ov2_t5
ov2_t3 ~~ ov2_t4 + ov2_t5
ov2_t4 ~~ ov2_t5

ov3_t1 ~~ ov3_t2 + ov3_t3 + ov3_t4 + ov3_t5
ov3_t2 ~~ ov3_t3 + ov3_t4 + ov3_t5
ov3_t3 ~~ ov3_t4 + ov3_t5
ov3_t4 ~~ ov3_t5

# THRESHOLDS FOR BINARY (OBSERVED) VARIABLE 'endo2'

endo2_t1 | tau_d1*t1
endo2_t2 | tau_d1*t1
endo2_t3 | tau_d1*t1
endo2_t4 | tau_d1*t1
endo2_t5 | tau_d1*t1

#####################################
### STRUCTURAL MODEL ###

# REGRESSIONS
# [I ran these unconstrained first and then slowly added constraints (they held).]

endo1_t1 ~ tic1
endo1_t2 ~ auto1*endo1_t1 + eff11*endo2_t1 + eff21*endo3_t1 + exo1*tic1
endo1_t3 ~ auto1*endo1_t2 + eff11*endo2_t2 + eff21*endo3_t2 + exo1*tic1
endo1_t4 ~ auto1*endo1_t3 + eff11*endo2_t3 + eff21*endo3_t3 + exo1*tic1
endo1_t5 ~ auto1*endo1_t4 + eff11*endo2_t4 + eff21*endo3_t4 + exo1*tic1

endo2_t1 ~ tic1
endo2_t2 ~ auto2*endo2_t1 + eff12*endo1_t1 + eff22*endo3_t1 + exo2*tic1
endo2_t3 ~ auto2*endo2_t2 + eff12*endo1_t2 + eff22*endo3_t2 + exo2*tic1
endo2_t4 ~ auto2*endo2_t3 + eff12*endo1_t3 + eff22*endo3_t3 + exo2*tic1
endo2_t5 ~ auto2*endo2_t4 + eff12*endo1_t4 + eff22*endo3_t4 + exo2*tic1

endo3_t1 ~ tic1
endo3_t2 ~ auto3*endo3_t1 + eff13*endo1_t1 + eff23*endo2_t1 + exo3*tic1
endo3_t3 ~ auto3*endo3_t2 + eff13*endo1_t2 + eff23*endo2_t2 + exo3*tic1
endo3_t4 ~ auto3*endo3_t3 + eff13*endo1_t3 + eff23*endo2_t3 + exo3*tic1
endo3_t5 ~ auto3*endo3_t4 + eff13*endo1_t4 + eff23*endo2_t4 + exo3*tic1

# COVARIANCES

endo1_t1 ~~ endo2_t1 + endo3_t1
endo1_t2 ~~ endo2_t2 + endo3_t2
endo1_t3 ~~ endo2_t3 + endo3_t3
endo1_t4 ~~ endo2_t4 + endo3_t4
endo1_t5 ~~ endo2_t5 + endo3_t5

endo2_t1 ~~ endo3_t1
endo2_t2 ~~ endo3_t2
endo2_t3 ~~ endo3_t3
endo2_t4 ~~ endo3_t4
endo2_t5 ~~ endo3_t5

# INTERCEPTS
# [Here, again, I ran them al unconstrained first and constrained later.]

endo1_t1 ~ 1
endo1_t2 ~ int1*1
endo1_t3 ~ int1*1
endo1_t4 ~ int1*1
endo1_t5 ~ int1*1

endo2_t1 ~ 1
endo2_t2 ~ int2*1
endo2_t3 ~ int2*1
endo2_t4 ~ int2*1
endo2_t5 ~ int2*1

endo3_t1 ~ 1
endo3_t2 ~ int3*1
endo3_t3 ~ int3*1
endo3_t4 ~ int3*1
endo3_t5 ~ int3*1

'

# [Used WLSMV and pairwise missing because of the ordinal variables.]

fit.model.1 <- sem(model.1, data=data, estimator="WLSMV", missing="pairwise", parameterization="delta",
        ordered=c("ov1_t1","ov1_t2","ov1_t3","ov1_t4","ov1_t5",
            "ov2_t1","ov2_t2","ov2_t3","ov2_t4","ov2_t5",
            "ov3_t1","ov3_t2","ov3_t3","ov3_t4","ov3_t5",
            "endo2_t1","endo2_t2","endo2_t3","endo2_t4","endo2_t5"))


Thank you so much for any help with my model and helping to answer my questions. It's much appreciated!

Kind regards,
Laurens Reumers

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Checking CLPM syntax for possible design errors
parts: - One of them ('endo2') is a binary observed variable

This will be a problem because results will differ across (arbitrary) identification constraints.  Try fitting an AR model just to that variable (on 5 occasions), once with parameterization="delta" and once with parameterization="theta".  Compare the standardized solutions and notice they are not the same.  If you have df>0 (e.g., because the AR paths are equal), you will also have different fit stats, proving the models are not equivalent.  The reason is that the latent-response scales are not linked across time, and there is no way to do so with only 1 threshold per item that you can constrain to equality over time.  To obtain a solution, all you can do is pretend that it is reasonable to assume either marginal or residual variances (delta or theta) are equal over time, neither of which is likely to be true.  Linking scales over time would require 2 thresholds, as discussed in this article about growth-curve models.  

Mehta, P. D., Neale, M. C., & Flay, B. R. (2004). Squeezing interval change from ordinal panel data: Latent growth curves with ordinal outcomes. Psychological Methods, 9(3), 301–333. https://doi.org/10.1037/1082-989X.9.3.301
I tested measurement invariance step-by-step and that seemed all good (factor loadings, intercepts, thresholds).

Hopefully not in that order.  Without constraints on thresholds to link scales (of endo1 indicators) across occasions, then there is no basis for comparing/equating loadings over time.  Constrain thresholds first, freeing the intercepts and (residual or marginal) variances after Time 1 because those constraints are not needed for identification any more.  

semTools::measEq.syntax() is a helpful tool to build models for these complex cases.  Find references on its help page, especially Wu & Estabrook (2016).
1. Are there any clear mistakes in the syntax below? Did I misunderstand how to do anything?
See comments above and below.

2. When constraining the intercepts to equality over time, can I leave the intercepts of t1 alone? These variables are not exogenous (only due to the sole effect from the TIC) but their intercepts are of course very different from those of t2 to t5. It would seem strange to try to include them in the equality constraints.

Not sure why you would want to constrain the intercepts to equality over time, but I agree that Time 1 does not have the same interpretation, so exclude that from the constrained set.  But you should still fix Time-1 intercepts to 0 (for identification).

endo1_t1 ~ 0*1
endo2_t1 ~ 0*1 

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

Thank you for your response. It is very helpful (as always, I might say).

Again, thank you for your help. It helped me proceed and fix those issues that were present in the model.

I got - as expected - different results by applying the different parameterizations when I want to estimate an AR model for the binary variable over time. I am fixing the only threshold at each occasion to zero and constraining the underlying variance to one - that should be coherent with the "delta" parameterization, to ensure the identification of the auxiliary model linking the observed binary to the underlying variables. When I try to fit the AR model for a categorical variable - with four categories - still I encounter these differences in the fit. 

I know that is expected but I am struggling a bit to understand (theoretically) - in this specific case - what determines that difference using the two parameterization and how to select one parameterization over the other a priori. 

Thanks a lot!
Silvia

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Checking CLPM syntax for possible design errors
parts:
with four categories - still I encounter these differences in the fit. 

I know that is expected but I am struggling a bit to understand (theoretically) - in this specific case - what determines that difference using the two parameterization and how to select one parameterization over the other a priori.

With more than 1 threshold, you can disentangle changes in the intercept/mean from changes in the (residual/marginal) variance.  This requires constraining threshold to equality across time (and testing whether those constraints hold), at which point you can freely estimate the intercepts and residual variances (theta: ~~ operator) or scaling factors (delta: ~*~ operator) on all occasions except the first (when they remain fixed to 0 and 1 for identification).  As long as your model is correctly specified, the different parameterizations should be statistically equivalent.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
